questions.stem:
consider the elementary reaction
$\mathrm{A(g) + B(g) \rightarrow C(g) + D(g)}$
If the volume of reaction mixture is suddenly reduced to $\frac{1}{3}$ of its initial volume, the reaction rate will become 'x' times of the original reaction rate. The value of x is :
questions.solution:
$R_{1} = K[A]^{1}[B]^{1}$
$R_{1} = K\left[\frac{n_{A}}{V}\right]^{1}\left[\frac{n_{B}}{V}\right]^{1}$
$R_{2} = K\left[\frac{3n_{A}}{V}\right]^{1}\left[\frac{3n_{B}}{V}\right]^{1}$
$R_{2} = 9R_{1}$

questions.stem:
Identify correct conversion during acidic hydrolysis from the following :
(A) starch gives galactose.
(B) cane sugar gives equal amount of glucose and fructose.
(C) milk sugar gives glucose and galactose.
(D) amylopectin gives glucose and fructose.
(E) amylose gives only glucose.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
(A) Starch $\xrightarrow{\mathrm{H^+/H_2O}}$ Glucose
(B) Cane sugar $\xrightarrow{\mathrm{H^+/H_2O}}$ glucose + fructose
(Sucrose) 50% 50%
(C) Milk sugar $\xrightarrow{\mathrm{H^+/H_2O}}$ glucose + galactose
(Lactose)
(D) Amylopectin $\xrightarrow{\mathrm{H^+/H_2O}}$ Glucose
(E) Amylose $\xrightarrow{\mathrm{H^+/H_2O}}$ Glucose
So, correct options are B, C and E only

questions.stem: The product B formed in the following reaction sequence is :

Concentrated nitric acid is labelled as 75% by mass. The volume in mL of the solution which contains 30 g of nitric acid is ___________.
Given : Density of nitric acid solution is 1.25 g/mL
questions.solution:
% w/w of $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ = 75%
means 100 gm of solution containing 75 g of $\mathrm{HNO_3}$
& $\left(\frac{\mathrm{gm}}{\mathrm{ml}}\right)_{\mathrm{solution}} = 1.25 = \frac{100\ \mathrm{gm}}{V}$
$V_{\mathrm{ml}}$ of 100 gm solution $= \frac{100}{1.25}$ ml
$\because$ 75 gm of $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ present in $\frac{100}{1.25}$ ml solution
$\therefore$ 30 gm of $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ present in
$\frac{100}{1.25 \times 75} \times 30 = 32$ ml solution

questions.stem: For bacterial growth in a cell culture, growth law is very similar to the law of radioactive decay. Which of the following graphs is most suitable to represent bacterial colony growth ?
questions.solution:
Because no. of bacteria initial $= N_{0}$
and No. of bacteria at any time $t = N$
Since bacterial growth is given as

questions.stem:
Which of the following is/are not correct with respect to energy of atomic orbitals of hydrogen atom?
(A) $1s < 2p < 3d < 4s$
(B) $1s < 2s = 2p < 3s = 3p$
(C) $1s < 2s < 2p < 3s < 3p$
(D) $1s < 2s < 4s < 3d$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
For single electron species energy only depends on 'n' (principal quantum number)
So energy of $2s = 2p$
and energy of $3d < 4s$

questions.stem:
Consider the following data :
Heat of formation of $\mathrm{CO_2(g)} = -393.5\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$
Heat of formation of $\mathrm{H_2O(l)} = -286.0\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$
Heat of combustion of benzene $= -3267.0\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$
The heat of formation of benzene is _____ $\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$. (Nearest integer)
questions.solution:
$\Delta H_{f}[\mathrm{CO_2(g)}] = -393.5$ kJ / mole
$\Delta H_{f}[\mathrm{H_2O(\ell)}] = -286.0$ kJ / mole
$\Delta H_{c}[\mathrm{C_6H_6}] = -3267.0$ kJ / mole
$\Delta H_{f}\ \mathrm{C_6H_6} = (?)$
$$\mathrm{C_6H_6 + \frac{15}{2}O_2(g) \longrightarrow 6CO_2(g) + 3H_2O(\ell)}$$
$\Delta H_{R} = \Delta H_{C} = \Sigma\Delta H_{f}(P) - \Sigma\Delta H_{f}(R)$
$-3267 = 6 \times (-393.5) + 3(-286) - \Delta H_{f}(\mathrm{C_6H_6})$
$\Delta H_{f}(\mathrm{C_6H_6}) = 48$ kJ/mole

questions.stem:
Electrolysis of 600 mL aqueous solution of NaCl for 5 min changes the pH of the solution to 12.
The current in Amperes used for the given electrolysis is ____. (Nearest integer).
questions.solution:
Electrolysis of NaCl is
$\mathrm{NaCl + H_2O\,(aq) \rightarrow NaOH\,(aq) + \frac{1}{2}Cl_2(g) + \frac{1}{2}H_2(g)}$
Since during electrolysis pH changes to 12
So $[\mathrm{OH^{-}}] = 10^{-2}$ and $[\mathrm{H^{+}}] = 10^{-12}$
So by Faraday law
Gram amount of substance deposited = Amount of electricity passed
$10^{-2} \times \frac{600}{1000} \times 96500 = I \times t$
$\frac{10^{-2} \times 600}{1000} \times 96500 = I \times 5 \times 60$
$I = \frac{10^{-2} \times 600 \times 96500}{1000 \times 5 \times 60}$
$I = 1.93$ ampere
So, $I = 2$ ampere (nearest integer)

$\mathrm{O_2^{+}} \rightarrow$ 1 unpaired electrons according to MOT

$\mathrm{NO_2} \rightarrow$ odd electron species

$\Rightarrow$ Tetrahedral, Paramagnetic with 2 unpaired electrons
